claims.text: Adding 1–2 at.% Pt during synthesis induces selective Pt surface segregation in multi-element HEA nanoparticles.
Selective Pt segregation forms a stabilizing Pt-enriched surface layer.
The Pt-enriched surface layer reduces atomic mobility and deleterious elemental diffusion.
The Pt-enriched layer preserves the nanoparticles' near-equiatomic structure under catalytic operation at 773–1173 K and thermoelectric operation at 473–1923 K.
Undoped near-equiatomic Fe–Co–Ni–Cu–Al nanoparticles have a disordered but chemically homogeneous interior after synthesis.
A Pt-enriched surface layer acts as a barrier to surface-atom diffusion and inter-element mixing.
Pt has lower surface energy than the other relevant constituents of the proposed HEA nanoparticles.
The lower surface energy of Pt causes dilute Pt to migrate preferentially to the nanoparticle surface during synthesis.
The resulting Pt surface layer restricts the mobility of adjacent atoms.
Restricted atomic mobility limits phase separation and elemental segregation during high-temperature exposure.
Pt-doped nanoparticles will retain a more homogeneous internal composition than undoped nanoparticles.
Pt-doped nanoparticles will exhibit lower degradation rates and less elemental segregation than undoped nanoparticles.
Pt-doped nanoparticles will show improved catalytic performance relative to undoped nanoparticles.
Pt-doped nanoparticles will show improved thermoelectric performance relative to undoped nanoparticles.
Undoped nanoparticles will undergo higher rates of surface diffusion, inter-element segregation, and structural degradation under the same high-temperature conditions.
The proposed stabilization mechanism is effective specifically in the 1–2 at.% Pt regime when synthesis favors surface segregation.
